gods.zeus: He stands above both sides. {{1|He promises Thetis to help the Trojans until the Achaeans honour Achilles.}}
gods.hera: Wife of Zeus. She hates Troy and wants the city to fall.
gods.athena: Daughter of Zeus. She protects Achilles, Diomedes and Odysseus.
gods.poseidon: Brother of Zeus, god of the sea. He holds a grudge against Troy: he built its walls for King Laomedon and was never paid.
gods.hephaestus: God of fire and smith of the gods, son of Hera.
gods.thetis: A sea goddess, mother of Achilles. She is not among the fighting gods, but she does everything for her son.
gods.apollo: God of the bow. He guards Troy from the first book on.
gods.artemis: Sister of Apollo, goddess of the hunt.
gods.aphrodite: Goddess of love, mother of Aeneas. She protects Paris.
gods.xanthos: The river of Troy. The gods call it Xanthus, men call it Scamander.

godsIntro: The sides are the ones Homer lists in Book 20, lines 31–40.

troy.name: The royal house of Troy
troy.note: As Aeneas tells it in Book 20, lines 215–240. Lycaon and Polydorus are Priam’s sons by Laothoe, not by Hecuba.

atreus.name: The sons of Atreus
atreus.note: The two brothers lead the expedition. Helen is the wife of Menelaus.

aeacus.name: The line of Achilles
aeacus.note: Aeacus is a son of Zeus (Book 21, line 189).

telamon.name: The sons of Telamon
telamon.note: Ajax and Teucer are half-brothers, with the same father. Later tradition makes Telamon a brother of Peleus. Homer does not say so.

nestor.name: The line of Nestor
nestor.note: Nestor is the oldest of the Achaean kings.

diomedes.name: The line of Diomedes
diomedes.note: {{6|Oeneus once had Bellerophon as his guest (Book 6, lines 215–221). That is why Diomedes and Glaucus do not fight.}}

lycia.name: The line of Glaucus and Sarpedon
lycia.note: Glaucus tells it to Diomedes in Book 6, lines 152–206.

familiesIntro: A name with a dot leads to that person’s home on the map.

days.waiting: Achilles stays apart; the gods are away
days.burial: A truce to bury the dead
days.battle2: Second day of battle and the night after

daysNote: The count of days is approximate: depending on how you count, it comes to between 50 and 54.

achilles.about: The strongest of the Achaeans, leader of the Myrmidons.

agamemnon.about: King of Mycenae and commander of the expedition.

menelaus.about: King of Sparta, husband of Helen. The war is fought for his sake.

odysseus.about: King of Ithaca, the most cunning of the Achaeans.

ajax.about: The strongest fighter after Achilles, with a huge shield.

ajax_lesser.about: Leader of the Locrians, a fast runner.

diomedes.about: King of Argos, young and fearless.

nestor.about: The old king of Pylos, adviser of the Achaeans.

patroclus.about: The closest friend of Achilles. He was born in Opus and brought up in Phthia.

idomeneus.about: King of Crete, grandson of Minos.

hector.about: Son of Priam, the defender of Troy.

paris.about: Son of Priam. He took Helen from Sparta.

aeneas.about: Leader of the Dardanians, son of a goddess.

sarpedon.about: King of the Lycians, son of Zeus.

glaucus.about: Leader of the Lycians together with Sarpedon.

helen.about: Wife of Menelaus, now in Troy with Paris.

andromache.about: Wife of Hector, daughter of King Eetion.

hecuba.about: Queen of Troy, wife of Priam.
